routes.name: ETA-IL Electronic Travel Authorization
routes.summary: Online travel authorization that visitors from visa-exempt countries need before flying to Israel (required since January 2025). Lets you stay up to 90 days per visit for tourism or business.

other: Must be a citizen of a visa-exempt country.
Passport valid at least 3 months from arrival.
Visit of 90 days or less, no work or medical purpose.
Not needed for Israeli citizens, holders of an Israeli ID number, or holders of Israeli visas B1, B3, B4, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5.
Approval does not guarantee entry. Border control makes the final call.

stay.note: Per visit. Authorization valid up to 2 years or until the passport expires, whichever is first.

routes.name: eVisa B/2 Tourist Visa
routes.summary: Online B/2 tourist visa for citizens of visa-required countries. Approval comes by email, and some people may be asked to visit the nearest Israeli consulate.

other: Must be a citizen of a country that needs a visa for Israel.
Needs passport copy, recent photo, round trip ticket, health insurance valid in Israel, proof of where you will stay, and proof of funds (3 months of bank statements or similar).
Approval does not guarantee entry.

stay.note: Visa validity up to 90 days per the consul. Stay length set by border control on arrival.

routes.name: B/2 Tourist Visa
routes.summary: Tourist visa for tourism, medical tourism, business meetings or short non-academic study. Usually single entry and valid three months from issue. No work allowed.

other: For nationalities that need a visa. Visa-exempt citizens use the ETA-IL instead.
Former foreign workers in agriculture, construction or caregiving can apply for a B/2 only one year after leaving Israel, even from a visa-exempt country.

stay.note: Usually single entry, valid three months from the day granted.

routes.name: B/1 Work Visa
routes.summary: B/1 work visas for foreign workers in industry, welfare, construction and agriculture, plus a separate B/1 foreign expert visa. Your employer applies in Israel and approval is sent to the consulate.

other: Request is submitted in Israel to the Interior Ministry (PIBA) by the employer, not by you.
Visa is for a limited period of work.
Fees, durations and expert criteria not confirmed. gov.il pages were blocked by a bot check.

routes.name: A/2 Student Visa
routes.summary: Student visa for study at an institution recognized by the Council for Higher Education, the VOLCANY Centre program, or the BA in Business Administration at the China-Israel Institute.

other: Needs acceptance at one of the institutions or programs named above.
Fees, duration and documents not confirmed. gov.il pages were blocked by a bot check.

routes.name: Law of Return (Aliyah)
routes.summary: People who qualify under the Law of Return enter on a new-immigrant visa and become Israeli citizens. Status is granted by the Ministry of Aliyah and Integration, and you need documents proving Jewish status under the law.

other: Needs documents proving Jewish status in line with the Law of Return, plus birth certificates and proof of family status.
Exact family-tie rules (children, grandchildren, spouses) and dual citizenship rules not confirmed from an official page.
The Ministry guide PDF would not load as text in the browser pass on 2026-11-11, so this was not re-confirmed.

sources.label: Ministry of Aliyah and Integration, Guide for the New Immigrant

routes.name: Returning Resident Status
routes.summary: For people who lived abroad two or more years and are coming back to Israel permanently. Status comes from the Ministry of Aliyah and Integration.

other: Based on the Ministry's new immigrant guide. Full conditions not confirmed.
The Ministry guide PDF would not load as text in the browser pass on 2026-11-11, so this was not re-confirmed.

routes.summary: Foreign spouses of Israelis apply through the Population and Immigration Authority in a staged process that leads to permanent status.

other: Stage lengths and conditions not confirmed.
